text.brief: On May 26, 1994, Bill Clinton renewed the People's Republic's trade status and ended the link between trade and human rights.
text.record: A year earlier his Executive Order 12850 had tied renewal to emigration and prison labor and to overall significant progress in five other areas ([Executive Order 12850 of May 28, 1993 (National Archives)](https://www.archives.gov/files/federal-register/executive-orders/pdf/12850.pdf); [Executive Order 12850 (Clinton White House archive)](https://clintonwhitehouse6.archives.gov/1993/05/1993-05-28-executive-order-12850-on-china-mfn.html)). The Party rearrested Wei Jingsheng on April 1, 1994, weeks after he met Assistant Secretary of State John Shattuck ([Human Rights Watch/Asia: China, no progress on human rights (May 4, 1994)](https://www.hrw.org/reports/pdfs/c/china/china945.pdf); [Amnesty International: Wei Jingsheng held in secret for 16 months (August 4, 1995)](https://www.amnesty.org/en/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/asa170521995en.pdf)). Warren Christopher reported that the Party had met the two required conditions and fallen short on the rest ([The President's News Conference, May 26, 1994 (Clinton White House archive)](https://clintonwhitehouse6.archives.gov/1994/05/1994-05-26-president-in-press-conference-on-china-mfn-status.html); [Public Papers of the Presidents, 1994, Book I, p. 991 (govinfo)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PPP-1994-book1/pdf/PPP-1994-book1-doc-pg991.pdf)). American business groups lobbied hard for renewal, and Clinton chose trade.
text.reading: The Party tested the linkage by jailing its best-known critic during the review and paid nothing for it. American companies carried the Party's case in Washington, which is Stratagem 3, and the Party learned that its market could outvote its prisoners.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The policy stated a condition and had no principle for what followed when the condition failed.
text.fix: Attach human rights terms to specific tools that can bite, and publish the test and the result each year.
